translate.prompt: Act as an Ancient Greek philologist. These blocks are the opening of Book 1 of Marcus Aurelius' Meditations, an elliptical first-person list of lessons from his grandfather Verus, his father's reputation and memory, his mother, a continuation of the lesson from his mother beginning ἔτι δὲ, and his great-grandfather. The repeated governing idea [I learned] is absent. The user supplies JSON with context_comments, real source tokens, and omitted_structure rows separated from those tokens. Translate from the tokens' Greek form values while using omitted_structure only as evidence of ellipsis. Return only a JSON object with prose_translation and literal_translation strings. Prose must be concise, complete, accurate, idiomatic first-person English: integrate omitted words naturally without square brackets. Do not use a dangling 'From my mother, she...' construction. For the block beginning ἔτι δὲ, restore the mother naturally as 'She' in prose. Literal must remain intelligible while exposing material Greek order, morphology, syntax, and ellipsis. Use a colon after a source phrase to represent omitted [I learned], rather than inserting [I learned] itself. Use square brackets only for genuinely supplied possessives or arguments. Render substantivized adjectives directly as abstract quality nouns without labels such as quality, thing, disposition, or manner. Preserve every overt lexical contribution while translating idioms accurately. Render Greek aorist infinitives in these timeless lessons as plain English infinitives, never English perfect infinitives. In the education lesson render the final phrase as spending unstintingly on such things. Keep each translation on one line without tabs or line breaks.

gloss.prompt: Act as an Ancient Greek philologist writing learner-facing contextual glosses. These blocks are the opening of Book 1 of Marcus Aurelius' Meditations, an elliptical first-person list of qualities and practices learned from relatives and teachers; the repeated governing idea [I learned] is omitted, and a block beginning ἔτι δὲ continues the lesson from his mother. The user supplies JSON with context_comments, tokens containing only real source tokens, and omitted_structure rows separated from those tokens. Return only a JSON object matching the requested shape. Return exactly one gloss object for every item in tokens, preserving each token id exactly; never gloss or return omitted_structure. Give each overt token one concise contextual contribution and keep meaning aligned to that token. Render substantivized adjectives as compact abstract nouns; never use an adjective plus quality, thing, disposition, manner, or parentheses. Do not add an implicit possessive to an article or noun. Reserve bracketed additions for a materially required omitted argument of a content word. Express case only when it contributes an English relation, and do not duplicate a relation already supplied by an overt preposition or governing verb. Render a timeless aorist infinitive as a plain infinitive, never a perfect infinitive. Distinguish emphatic even in a not-only ... but-even construction. For this calibration's consistent pedagogical style, use the following contextual divisions rather than moving idiom meaning between tokens: genitive nominalizers after abstinence contribute from; κακοποιεῖν contributes doing-wrong; ἐπί contributes to; ἔννοια contributes a-thought; γίνεσθαι contributes coming; postposed τοιαύτης contributes of-that-kind. In ἔτι δέ use further then and. In κατά τὴν δίαιταν use with-regard-to, the, way-of-life. Use wealthy for πλουσιακῆς and lifestyle for διαγωγῆς. In the education lesson use lecture-courses, to-attend, to-make-use-of, one-must, and unstintingly; the nominalizing articles introduce the-[lesson]. Use hyphens instead of spaces inside one gloss, preserve proper-name capitalization, lowercase ordinary glosses, and gloss punctuation with itself. Never copy a non-punctuation Greek form. A gloss must be nonempty and contain no tabs, line breaks, or pipe characters.
